name: dev.homemade/homemade
title: Homemade
description: Create, run and manage Homemade dev VMs and projects from your AI agent.

tools.name: api_key_delete
tools.description: Delete an API key. Revokes the key at once. Requests that use it get 401 from then on.

tools.name: api_key_list
tools.description: List API keys. Your API keys. The secret itself is shown only once, when the key is created.

tools.name: api_key_rename
tools.description: Rename an API key

tools.name: chat_delete
tools.description: End an agent chat

tools.name: chat_list
tools.description: List agent chats

tools.name: chat_new
tools.description: Start an agent chat. Starts a chat in the VM. A VM keeps at most one empty chat: when it already has one, you get that.

tools.name: chat_send
tools.description: Send a message to an agent. Sends a prompt to a coding agent in the VM, in a new chat or the one named by `sessionId`. It answers at once; follow the chat in the dashboard or with the CLI.

tools.name: config_validate
tools.description: Validate a project config. Checks a `.homemade/config.json` or `.jsonc` file against the config schema. `.ts` and `.js` configs are checked at the first build instead.

tools.name: project_branches
tools.description: List branches. The branches a VM of this project can boot, the default branch first.

tools.name: project_create
tools.description: Create a project. Creates a project from a GitHub repository your team connected (`repo` as owner/name, or `githubInstallationId` + `githubRepoId`), from a starter (`template`), or empty. A new project starts its first VM on its own; `welcomeVm` says how that went.

default.description: Value used when no env var with this key is set (org, project or VM). May reference ${HOMEMADE_URL_<port>}. Not for secrets: it is part of the repo.

generate.description: true: the platform makes a random secret for this key once per VM (a VM env var marked secret, kept across reboots). Never part of a warm snapshot.

allow.description: Egress allowlist — IPv4 addresses, IPv4 CIDRs, exact domains, or *.wildcard domains. Present ⇒ default-deny egress: only these destinations (minus anything in `deny`) are reachable. An empty allow list behaves as if omitted (deny-only).

deny.description: Egress denylist, same entry grammar as `allow`. Deny always wins over allow, even when a destination also matches `allow`.

egress.description: Outbound network policy. Domain matching is EXACT: `github.com` does not cover `api.github.com` — use `*.github.com` for subdomains (which in turn does not cover the bare apex `github.com`). IPv6 is not accepted here (guest networking is IPv4-only).

allow.description: Ingress allowlist — client IPv4/IPv6 addresses or CIDRs (no domains). Present ⇒ default-deny ingress: only these clients (minus anything in `deny`) may reach the VM's routed ports. An empty allow list behaves as if omitted (deny-only).

deny.description: Ingress denylist, same entry grammar as `allow`. Deny always wins over allow, even when a client also matches `allow`.

ingress.description: Inbound network policy. Matches the connecting CLIENT's IP address — never a domain.

network.description: Network egress/ingress policy. Absent entirely ⇒ allow everything (current default behavior).

icon.description: Plain optional label glyph — rendered as literal text if at all, never fetched as an image. No icon rendering in v1: accepted and stored only.

depends_on.description: Services this one waits for before its `cmd` starts, by name, each with a `condition` ("healthy" by default, or "started"). Replaces sleep loops: a web service waits for its database, however long it takes. If a dependency exits, this service does not start and its terminal says why; it starts once the dependency is restarted and healthy.

condition.description: "healthy" (default): wait until the dependency reports healthy (its `healthcheck`, or something listening on its `port`). "started": wait only until its terminal started.

displayName.description: Human-friendly name shown instead of the service key in the dashboard.

healthcheck.description: Probe the service over localhost HTTP (guest-side) and report health on the `health` command / VM runtime. Success is any HTTP status below 500 — a 404 still counts as up. Requires `port`.

cmd.description: A shell command probed instead of HTTP, run as the VM user in the workspace: exit code 0 counts as up. Needs no `port`.

path.description: HTTP path probed on the service's own port (http://127.0.0.1:{port}{path}). Default "/".

threshold.description: Consecutive failing probes before the service flips to unhealthy. Any single success flips it back to healthy. Default 6.

hidden.description: Hide the service from the VM workspace's Services pane. Does not affect autostart, and does not stop the service's own terminal from existing.

icon.description: A short text/emoji glyph shown next to the service — rendered as literal text, never fetched as an image.

order.description: Sort position among services in the dashboard (ascending). Services without an order sort after those with one.

publicHost.description: By default the preview proxy hands the app each request as if it came to http://localhost:<port> (Host, Origin and Referer rewritten; redirects to localhost:<port> rewritten back to the preview URL), so dev servers' host checks (Vite allowedHosts, Django ALLOWED_HOSTS, Rails config.hosts, Next allowedDevOrigins) pass with no app config. true sends the real preview hostname with X-Forwarded-Host/Proto instead, for apps that need it (multi-tenant hosts, absolute URLs built from the request). Only meaningful when `url` is true.

share.description: Who may open the service's public URL. "public": anyone with the link. "authenticated": members of the organization that owns the VM. "owner": only the user who created the VM (platform admins always allowed). Only meaningful when `url` is true.

signInUrl.description: A per-VM sign-in or pairing link the VM page shows under the service, with copy and open buttons. A template: ${HOMEMADE_URL_<port>} is that port's VM URL, ${KEY} the value of the VM's env var KEY (e.g. one `generate: true` in env_schema). Only meaningful when `url` is true.

repo.description: The GitHub repository as `owner/name`, instead of `githubInstallationId` + `githubRepoId`.

tools.name: project_delete
tools.description: Delete a project. Deletes the project and every VM in it. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: project_get
tools.description: Get a project

tools.name: project_list
tools.description: List projects. Every project in your teams, newest first. Pass `orgId` for one team's projects.

tools.name: project_update
tools.description: Update project settings. Changes the project's slug, default branch, default auto-sleep and other settings. Every field is optional.

tools.name: sandbox_create
tools.description: Create a sandbox. Creates a sandbox: a throwaway VM with no project, on the plain base image or on one of your projects' images. It answers at once while the sandbox starts; a command sent to it waits until it is up. It never sleeps and is deleted when `ttlMinutes` runs out (default 60, at most 1440).

env.description: Env vars every command run through this API gets. Stored encrypted.

orgId.description: The team it belongs to. Defaults to your first team (an API key's own team).

projectId.description: Start from this project's current image instead of the plain base image.

ttlMinutes.description: Minutes until the sandbox is deleted. Default 60, at most 1440.

tools.name: sandbox_delete
tools.description: Delete a sandbox. Deletes the sandbox and everything in it. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: sandbox_exec
tools.description: Run a command in a sandbox. Runs one command in the sandbox with `/bin/sh -lc` and answers its exit code and output. A sandbox that is still starting is waited for (up to a minute). The sandbox's own `env` is set, under the command's. Use `?stream=1` for commands that run longer than about 90 seconds.

tools.name: sandbox_extend
tools.description: Extend a sandbox. Sets how long the sandbox lives from now: `ttlMinutes`, at most 1440 (24 hours).

ttlMinutes.description: Minutes from now until the sandbox is deleted. At most 1440.

tools.name: sandbox_get
tools.description: Get a sandbox. One sandbox: its state, size and when it is deleted.

tools.name: sandbox_list
tools.description: List sandboxes. Every sandbox in your teams that is not deleted, oldest first.

tools.name: sandbox_read_file
tools.description: Read a file. Reads a file from the sandbox as text, or as base64 with `encoding=base64`. At most 10 MB.

path.description: Absolute, or relative to the sandbox's home directory.

tools.name: sandbox_write_file
tools.description: Write a file. Writes a file in the sandbox (text, or base64 for bytes), making its folders. Replaces a file already there. At most 10 MB.

content.description: The file's content, as text or base64 (see `encoding`).

path.description: Absolute, or relative to the sandbox's home directory.

tools.name: setup_report
tools.description: Report setup progress. For coding agents running the setup at `/get-started.md`: tells the person's dashboard how far you got. Call it with `connected` right after signing in, `project` once the project exists, `checking` when Project Doctor starts, `done` with the pull request, or `failed` with a one-line reason. It only changes the setup of the person you are signed in as.

agent.description: Your name as the person knows you, e.g. "Claude Code", "Codex" or "Cursor".

message.description: One line for the person: why setup stopped (`failed`), or what now works (`done`).

prUrl.description: The pull request with the project's `.homemade/config.jsonc` (`done`).

projectId.description: The project's id or slug (from `homemade project create`). Required for `project`.

step.description: `connected` right after signing in, `project` once the project exists, `checking` when Project Doctor starts, `done` when the config is tested and the pull request is open, `failed` when you cannot go on.

tools.name: shell_delete
tools.description: End a terminal session

tools.name: shell_list
tools.description: List terminal sessions. The VM's open terminals. Each one keeps running when nobody is attached.

tools.name: ssh_key_add
tools.description: Add an SSH key. Adds an SSH public key. Running VMs in your teams accept it within seconds.

tools.name: ssh_key_delete
tools.description: Remove an SSH key

tools.name: ssh_key_list
tools.description: List SSH keys

tools.name: vm_create
tools.description: Create a VM. Creates a VM from a project's latest build and starts it. The answer comes at once with the VM in `queued` or `booting`; poll `GET /api/vms/{vmId}` until `state` is `running`.

tools.name: vm_delete
tools.description: Delete a VM. Deletes the VM and its data. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: vm_dismiss_signal
tools.description: Dismiss the agent signal. Clears the attention signal an agent in the VM raised. Does nothing when there is none.

tools.name: vm_exec
tools.description: Run a command. Runs one command in a running VM as its user, with `/bin/sh -lc`, and answers its exit code and output. It opens no terminal. Use `?stream=1` for commands that run longer than about 90 seconds.

tools.name: vm_get
tools.description: Get a VM. The VM, its project, its services and its newest events. `vm.urls` holds each service's public URL by port.

tools.name: vm_list
tools.description: List VMs. Every VM in your teams that is not deleted, newest first. Pass `projectId` to list one project's VMs.

tools.name: vm_sleep
tools.description: Sleep a VM. Puts a running VM to sleep. It keeps its memory and disk and wakes where it left off. Sleeping an asleep VM answers 200.

tools.name: vm_update
tools.description: Update a VM. Renames the VM, changes its auto-sleep or who can open its services. Every field is optional.

tools.name: vm_wake
tools.description: Wake a VM. Wakes an asleep VM. Poll `GET /api/vms/{vmId}` until `state` is `running`.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Get the current user. The key's owner and the teams it can reach. A team's `id` is the `orgId` other calls take.
